craft_claim: Urgency decays with repetition within a text and across a corpus; sustained high-intensity urgency produces fatigue and reduced response, so the tone must yield to lower-intensity passages.

supporting_evidence.location: Cry Wolf: The Psychology of False Alarms, book thesis
supporting_evidence.note: Habituation to alarms lowers later response; the more often the alarm is raised, the cheaper each raising becomes.
Accurate repetition can reinforce, but indiscriminate repetition of high-intensity messages dilutes signal value; warning practice depends on reserve and differentiation of alerts.
Operational evidence that high alarm volume produces desensitization, supporting the claim that urgency has a saturation point.

scope: Sustained prose longer than a few paragraphs, and any publication stream with a recurring audience.
exceptions: Very short copy may sustain a single urgent beat without fatigue.
Genuine fast-developing crises can justify dense repetition for a bounded interval.
